1 دَاخَ , (S, A, L, K,) aor. يَدُوخُ, (S,) inf. n. دَوْخٌ, (L,) He (a man, S, A) was, or became, submissive, or abject, (S, A, L, K,) and lowly, or humble. (A, L.) ―
-b2- [Also (assumed tropical:) It (a man's head) was, or became, giddy, or vertiginous: used in this sense in the present day, and probably in ancient times: see 2.] ＝
-A2- As a trans. verb: see 2.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
